chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from Dharih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever five years pass for him and he does not make his way to his Lord while he is wealthy, indeed he is deprived."

key_terms.يَفِدْ: to make one's way / to travel (specifically for Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on delaying Hajj for five years if one is financially able?
ai.summary: In the Shia scholarly tradition, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the urgency of the Hajj obligation for the financially capable (al-musir), warning that a five-year delay without valid excuse leads to spiritual deprivation (mahroom). This timeframe reflects the juristic consensus on the maximum permissible postponement before the duty becomes incumbent upon the individual's immediate conscience.
